title: A remote handler that forwards too few arguments can silently turn one action into another
observation: Loot Goblins' server wired its shop RemoteEvent as OnServerEvent(player, action, id) -> handle(player, action, id), but the shop sends (action, slot, item) and handle accepts (player, action, a, b). For two versions every 'equip, slot, item' arrived as 'equip, slot' with a nil item, which the handler treats as taking the slot off, and replied ok. Unit tests of handle and of the ownership rules all passed; only purchases (which equip inside the handler) changed a look. A Studio playtest that equipped an already-owned pet through the real remote exposed it.
recommendation: Forward every argument (or use varargs) when one handler routes a remote to another, give each action an end-to-end test through the real remote that checks the replicated result (not only the reply), and treat an ok reply with no visible change as a bug signal.
applies_when: A RemoteEvent handler routes requests to another module
An action's absent argument has a meaning of its own (nil = remove, default, unequip)
limits: One code base; found by one AI in one Studio session

evidence.detail: Section 31, bug 1: equip replied ok while Pet and BoatClass did not change; after forwarding both arguments, WEAR and SAIL changed them and an outfit kept its name.
